appeal.letter:
Subject: Appeal Against Denial of Claim ID 92d32bde-6f58-766d-3b02-e72981ef571a – Pre‑Existing Disease Waiting Period

Claim Details:  
Patient Name: Jeraldine Santos Bins  
Policy: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Plan Code SGH‑SILVER)  
Policy Start Date: 22‑Nov‑2023  
Date of Service: 17‑Aug‑2026  
Encounter Class: Ambulatory (AMB)  
Diagnosis: Essential hypertension (first diagnosed 20‑Mar‑2026)  
Procedure: Referral to hypertension clinic  
Claim Amount: INR 2,067.80  

Grounds for Appeal:  
The denial cites D03 – Pre‑existing disease waiting period not completed. Under the policy definition, a Pre‑Existing Disease is a condition diagnosed within 48 months prior to the first policy start date. The patient’s hypertension was first diagnosed on 20‑Mar‑2026, which is after the policy start date of 22‑Nov‑2023. Accordingly, the condition does not meet the definition of a Pre‑Existing Disease and the waiting period does not apply [suraksha_silver_policy#5]. Consequently, the exclusion in Clause 4.2 is inapplicable because it applies only to conditions that satisfy the definition in Clause 2.2 [suraksha_silver_policy#11].

Clinical Necessity:  
Essential hypertension requires ongoing monitoring and management to prevent cardiovascular complications. The diagnosis is confirmed when blood pressure readings are ≥ 140/90 mmHg on two separate visits, as documented in the clinical guideline [hypertension#2]. A referral to a specialized hypertension clinic is a standard, evidence‑based step to achieve optimal blood pressure control and reduce risk of target‑organ damage. The treating physician will attach the relevant clinical notes confirming the diagnosis date and the need for the referral.

Reference to Denial Standards:  
According to the insurer’s own denial standards, the burden of proof for a Pre‑Existing Disease exclusion rests with the insurer, which must provide documentary evidence that the condition existed before the policy start date [claims_procedure_and_grievance#6]. No such evidence has been supplied; the claim records clearly show the diagnosis date post‑policy commencement.

Specific Request:  
In light of the above, we request that the denial be rescinded, the claim be re‑processed, and payment of INR 2,067.80 be made to the provider without further delay.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Insurance Desk (on behalf of the treating provider)

Pre-Existing Disease means any condition, ailment, injury or disease that was diagnosed by a physician, or for which medical advice or treatment was received, within 48 months PRIOR TO the first policy start date. citations.section: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Policy Wording) > 4. Waiting Periods > 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
citations.quote:
### 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
Expenses related to a Pre-Existing Disease (as defined in Clause 2.2) are covered only after 36 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. This waiting period applies ONLY to conditions meeting the definition in Clause 2.2.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C3. Standards for Denial > C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
citations.quote:
### C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies. For a Pre-Existing Disease denial, the insurer must show documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date.

citations.section: Essential Hypertension — Diagnosis and Monitoring > Diagnosis
citations.quote:
## Diagnosis
Hypertension is diagnosed when clinic blood pressure is ≥ 140/90 mmHg on two or more separate visits, ideally confirmed by home or ambulatory monitoring. The diagnosis date is the visit at which it was confirmed.
